title: Change in chronotype during physiological development in children and adolescents and investigation of mechanisms during puberty that influence metabolic balance.
summary:
This study analyses the 'internal clock' (chronotype) in children and adolescents during development, particularly during puberty, and its significance in the development of endocrine and metabolic diseases.

The objectives of the study are:
1) To evaluate chronotype in children and adolescents by analysing questionnaires, in order to assess the relevance of chronobiological aspects for the development and treatment of endocrine/metabolic diseases. The questionnaires focus on sleep/wake behaviour.

interventions.name: Cohort I (“Reference cohort”): recruitment of 100 healthy children/adolescents (50 male/ 50 female participants) without altered pubertal development (age range: 1-18 years).

Cohort II (“Altered puberty cohort”): 30 individuals each, with either precocious central puberty; premature thelarche, precocious adrenarche (age: boys younger than 9 years, females younger than 8 years) and delayed central puberty (age: boys older than 14 years, females older than 13 years); (sum
Cohort III (“Obesity cohort”): 200 male and 200 female individuals with obesity will be recruited (BMI above 95. percentile; age: 8-18 years).
Cohort IV: patients with rare endocrine diseases (e.g. congenital adrenal hyperplasia, genetic disturbances of hypothalamic hormone production and -action)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Female or male
2. Aged between 1 month and 18 years
3. Cohort 1 (‘reference cohort’): no chronic illness
4. Cohort 2 (‘cohort with altered pubertal development’): diagnosis of pubertas praecox or premature pubarche, premature thelarche or pubertas tarda
5. Cohort 3 (‘obesity cohort’): obesity (BMI above the 97th percentile)
6. Cohort 4 children with genetic diseases (e.g. obesity due to POMC deficiency or increased sex hormone production in congenital adrenal hyperplasia)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Ongoing participation in a drug trial, or if participation ended less than one month ago
2. Sleep disorders, periodic leg movements
3. Alcohol, tobacco, drug abuse
4. Flights across at least two time zones within the last four weeks prior to inclusion
5. Acute psychosocial stress situation
